meaningMnemonic: If you pick up your sword ( 刀 ) and see a drop ( 丶 ) of blood, it might mean you accidentally grabbed it by the blade . Blades are sharp, so be careful when you handle them — you don't want to get drops of blood everywhere.

We can see your rib cage, and bad shellfish are the ones to blame . These shellfish gave you terrible food poisoning, and now you're so emaciated that your rib cage is visible. Don't blame yourself for what you ate — blame the shellfish for doing this to you.

This radical is the same as the kanji, so it means half . This even looks like a few lines getting split in half. See how the top one is actually broken in half too? That's why this is the half radical.

There's something standing up on this head that's old. It's a mohawk . What other hairstyle stands straight up? Mohawks are also kind of old-school, as far as hairstyles go, which is why this mohawk stands straight up off an old guy's head.
A person is wondering where to go next , so they look at the big arrow above their head and start moving in the direction it points towards. Where will they end up next?
This radical is the same as the kanji, but "number in a series" is too long. Let's shorten it to number .

You want to compose some writing ( 文 ), but you also want to look at the moon ( 月 ). Well, why not make both activities simultaneous ? If you write while simultaneously looking at the moon, you'll probably come up with a cool romantic poem or something.
What's mama doing? It looks like she's dodging a spear . Do you see the spear rushing past her as she leaps backwards to avoid it? Phew, that was a close call! Not today, spear. Not today.

The blame radical and the blame kanji are the same, because you still blame those bad shellfish for giving you food poisoning and making your rib cage visible. Actually, you blame them so much that you're now formally asking them to take responsibility too. Hints You'll never stop blaming those shellfish for what they did to you. They must take responsibility for their actions!
readingMnemonic: One thing you can't blame the shellfish for is making you so darn sexy ( せき ). Even in your emaciated, food-poisoned state, you're still one of the sexiest people around. Hints You blame your parents for making you so sexy. Why'd they have to give you such sexy genes? They'd better take responsibility, 'cause it ain't easy living life as a sexy bombshell.

meaningMnemonic: Your magic yoga brush lets you build what's in your mind's eye. Hints You do the bridge pose, and in your mind you imagine your brush painting an actual bridge. When you open your eyes, there it is! A bridge has been built, leading straight to your front door.
readingMnemonic: You build a bridge. Immediately after, someone is climbing up onto it. It's Ken ( けん ) the samurai. He waves at you and says, "Did you build this? The craftsmanship is amazing." Hints It seems like Ken the samurai really appreciates your building skills.

meaningMnemonic: A winter tree is only a winter tree due to a clause in its tree contract. Hints The clause states the tree can only be a tree in winter, but not during other seasons. Once winter descends, the clause takes effect and it becomes a tree. (See how winter is descending on the tree from above in this kanji?) Go ahead and look at its contract — see the winter tree clause, right there, in fine print.
readingMnemonic: This clause was written into all trees' contracts by Joe ( じょう ), the large farmhand. Hints Joe noticed that the trees were getting too crowded, so he wrote up these clauses and added them to the trees' contracts. Now, the forests are less crowded, thanks to the little clause. Makes sense that a farmhand like Joe would do this, too. The fewer trees, the more farmland. It's good for folks like Joe.

meaningMnemonic: You see a tsunami that's simultaneous (with another tsunami, I assume) and you know the world is about to come to an end . Hints Imagine a tsunami simultaneously happening as the world comes to an end. Oh no, isn't there any way to stop this!?
readingMnemonic: Just as the world is about to come to an end , your cy borg ( さい ) appears and blocks it with its cyborg body! Hints So the world won't come to an end this one time, thanks to the cyborg you made. Though it doesn't look very good. The cyborg is beaten up and full of water. This might be the end for it...

meaningMnemonic: Beside your mouth you hold your cross as you pray for all your wishes to come true . Perhaps some divine power will grant what you wish for? Hints Picture yourself holding your cross right up next to your mouth as you speak your prayers. What will you wish to come true? It could be anything you want!
readingMnemonic: And if you really want your wish to come true , make sure to write it down in kana ! Hints Legend has it that writing down your wishes in kana will lead to higher chances of them actually coming true! Whether you go with hiragana or katakana is up to you, just make sure it's all in some form of kana.

meaningMnemonic: A grain woman is a woman who talks about grain with other women on a committee . Together they're known as the Committee of Grain Women. What does this committee discuss, you wonder. Hints Imagine what this committee of women could be coming together to discuss. Isn't grain just grain? Why do they need a whole committee?
readingMnemonic: Well, they formed this committee because ea gles ( い ) have been eating all the grain. The women meet as a committee and try to come up with ways to stop these pesky eagles from eating all the grain and leaving none for the humans. Hints Imagine a committee of women standing together in a field of grain, watching eagles swooping around. They take notes and mutter to one another about their options.

meaningMnemonic: You only have a few eye s so you need to conserve what's left. Hints You only have like, three eyes left. If you conserve them.
readingMnemonic: You're trying to conserve your eyes, when the Shou gun ( しょう ) marches by. He stops, sees you, and demands you give him your remaining eyes! But sir, I'm conserving what little I have left! Hints The Shougun stares down at you, eyes blazing, and you hand over all but one of your eyes. Now you really have to conserve, or you'll be blind. Thanks Shougun. I bet he has plenty of eyes, he didn't need yours.

meaningMnemonic: Cow s, using nothing more than a towel and a knife , have taken control of the world. Their system of control is brutal — payback for how we humans have treated them, I guess. Hints Imagine this new cow-controlled world — there are cows on every street corner, armed with towels and knives, intimidating all us humans into following their system.
readingMnemonic: It's time to take control back from the cows! Pull out your sa ber ( せい ) and fight back! Hints The cows' towels and knives won't stand a chance against your saber!

meaningMnemonic: If you use your fingers to point when you compare things you're really just throwing around criticism . You should never need to point fingers when you're just comparing things. If you're pointing and picking and being mean, that's criticism. Hints Some criticism is okay, as long as it's constructive and it helps the person get better. But when you start pointing fingers, it's time to step back and try to not be such a jerk.
readingMnemonic: If you're having trouble not giving out criticism , just think about how you would react if someone criticized you. You'd feel an embarrassed he at ( ひ ) rise throughout your body. That heat will cover your whole face. Hints Before you throw criticism around, imagine that embarrassed heat. You don't want to feel that way, so why would you do it to someone else?

meaningMnemonic: A lion harvesting rice uses an axe to cut off the tops of the stalks. The lion is roaming the rice fields using his axe to harvest the rice. He does so by cutting off the part of the rice stalks he needs. Hints Picture this lion on his hind legs, walking through a rice field. He’s holding an axe in one hand and acting like a human. See him cut off the plants and hear the whoosh of the axe as he cuts.
readingMnemonic: The lion will cut off rice stalks until dawn ( だん ). But at the first light of dawn, it will run and hide in the shade of the trees, cut off from the rice. Hints When dawn comes in Africa (it's a lion, so that's where he is) it gets too hot to be in the sun, so the lion gets cut off from his job of cutting things off.

meaningMnemonic: Both a leader and a king have a duty to protect their people. A good leader always protects his followers, and a good king always protects his subjects. This is their duty. Hints Imagine yourself being protected by your king and leader. They don’t really like you, but it is their duty to protect you. See them fighting off evil doers and taking bullets for your sake.
readingMnemonic: You’re the village nin compoop ( にん ), but the king and the leader still have a duty to protect you. Even a nincompoop is important to the kings and leaders of the world. Hints You’re a nincompoop. Even though you’re so nincompoopy, your king and leader still have a duty to protect you. Feel happy and content, despite your nincompoopery.

meaningMnemonic: If you look really close at your rib cage , you'll see what looks like millions of tiny little thread s. But those aren't threads — they're the essential element s of life as we know it. Hints These elements are the threads that tie together every living organism. You can see these elements especially well in large bones like the rib cage, but they're visible in other body parts too.
readingMnemonic: The essential element s of life need to be kept clean just like everything else, so you make sure to wash them with so ap ( そ ) every single day. This turns out to be pretty hard since the elements are shaped like tiny microscopic threads, but you do your best. Hints Imagine grabbing handfuls of the essential elements of life and trying to wash them with soap. They're slippery so you keep dropping clumps of them, and soap keeps going in your eyes..

meaningMnemonic: Seeing a mohawk in the winter means the enemy is nearby. You are from the dreadlock tribe and the mohawk tribe is your enemy. You’re deep in the heart of battle and winter has fallen. Now is the time to take out the enemy. Hints Picture yourself holed up in a winter encampment, waiting to strike at the mohawk wearing enemies. Feel the cold around you as you scan the horizon for mohawks.
readingMnemonic: You're kind of a techie ( てき ), so you have an advantage over your enemy . You're armed with night vision goggles and other cool tech gear as well. Being a techie certainly has its advantages. Hints Imagine yourself all teched out like the techie you are. Hear the beeps and boops of all the technology you have at your disposal as you search for more mohawk enemies.

meaningMnemonic: Sheep are always looking at the next animal, full of envy and jealousy . Hints Picture a sheep comparing itself to the next creature, and feeling deep envy and jealousy. Why does it feel that way?
readingMnemonic: The reason the sheep feels such envy and jealousy is that the next creature is a cen taur ( せん )! Who wouldn't be jealous of a creature as noble as a centaur? Hints Being a centaur is every sheep's dream, so they can't help feeling terrible jealousy when they see one.

meaningMnemonic: If you say a new weapon idea out loud, then it will be establish ed immediately. Hints Try it out: I want a stabbing weapon with extra weapons that can pop out on the sides. *POOF* You've established a new weapon. And it's been added to the official weapon wiki of the world.
readingMnemonic: Weapons have to be establish ed in sets ( せつ ). So you have to make another one that goes with it. Make them cohesive please. Hints Establish weapons in sets or the people who use them won't be able to match each other.

meaningMnemonic: You see a tree with a squid on it, so you get closer to examine it. Hints As you examine the tree and the squid in it, you think, "Huh, nope still weird." You should examine it further to find out what's going on.
readingMnemonic: You're sticking your face in really, really close to examine this little squid in the tree when Ken ( けん ) the samurai appears behind you. "There you are, squid! Thank you citizen, I've been looking all over for my little chum." Hints Imagine how many trees Ken examined before he found you both. Picture him putting his face really close to each one, then shedding a single tear when he realized this squid wasn't in it.

meaningMnemonic: An animal tries to eat your ear because it mistakes it for its feed . Maybe you shouldn't put your ears so close to the animal food — there's nothing to listen to down there besides wet, slobbery chewing sounds anyway. Hints Hear the sound of livestock munching away at their feed. Then, feel one of them chomp down on your ear. Ow!
readingMnemonic: You're walking by one of the animal pens with some feed when you hear, " Ay , sir ( えさ )! Ay, sir! Bring some of that animal food over here please." Did an animal just… talk to you? Hints Suddenly, you hear a chorus of animal voices erupt around you: "Ay, sir! Bring us some feed next, sir! Ay, sir! We want some animal food, sir!" When did these animals learn to talk???

meaningMnemonic: You have a scene going on inside your head . It is of a pair of horns on the ground atop a mountain . No. It is not just one pair of horns. It is many. So many that they create a giant hill atop the mountain, which is already pretty high. Hints Imagine this hill of horns on top of this mountain. This hill of horns makes it possible for you to get just high enough to touch the top of the sky.
readingMnemonic: How was standing atop this hill of horns on top of a mountain to touch the sky? Eh. It was oka y ( おか ), but that's about it. Hints Feel indifferent about this hill of horns on top of the mountain. It's all in your head anyways.

meaningMnemonic: The dirt mask is a mask which, when put on, will greatly increase the amount of dirt. Hints Imagine putting it on, and suddenly the dirt around you increases by quite a bit.
readingMnemonic: Use the dirt mask to increase the dirt around you. The zo mbies ( ぞう ) are trying to escape, so you just keep increasing the dirt on top of them so they can't get out. Hints Zombie hands keep coming out of the ground, but as long as you wear the mask and increase the dirt on top of them, they won't be able to escape their earthly prison.

meaningMnemonic: If a tree is growing out of a top hat you need to inspect it to find out why and how this happened. You should probably investigate the area too. I mean, how could a tree grow out of a top hat anyway? Seems suspicious. Hints Inspect the tree. Inspect the top hat. Did you find anything?
readingMnemonic: As you inspect the tree, you pick up a saw ( さ ) and start cutting it. You need to investigate how the tree and the top hat are connected, and a saw is the only way to do it properly. Hints Turns out the top hat was just decorative and the tree was growing out of the earth, like any other tree. Imagine your shame now. You should be more careful — don't be sawing trees willy nilly.

meaningMnemonic: I hereby cut your assets in half with a knife , says the judge . At someone's divorce proceedings. Ah, the oldest judge trick in the book. Hints If you can't decide who gets custody of the baby, the dog, the house, the car, the furniture, the savings, and the house plants, you have to leave it up to the judge. And the judge's judgment is that everything is cut in half with a knife. What an efficient judge.
readingMnemonic: This judge is Han ( はん ) Solo, so you know he's not going to back down. Hints Han Solo the judge is a very busy person, so he has to judge quickly and efficiently. He'll cut all your stuff perfectly in half before he wastes time listening to you argue about who earned what. Sure it's crude, but at least it's… equal?

meaningMnemonic: The leader of the cow tribe is too important to deal with small matter s and trivial affair s. Hints Picture this hoity-toity cow leader who thinks he’s too good for small matters and affairs. See him acting all fancy like he’s better than everyone else. The cow even moos with a fake British accent. How pretentious.
readingMnemonic: All of his affair s are taken care of by Ken ( けん ) the samurai, who he hired as his underling. Hints Picture Ken the samurai scooping poop for the leader of the cows, because that's a matter of poop and state.

meaningMnemonic: Building s hold festival s on special occasion s. Hints A festival can't be happening all the time. Then it wouldn't be special, it would just be a party building, so they can only happen on special occasions.
readingMnemonic: The occasion this time is to celebrate your wonderful cy borg ( さい ). It's about time you did something nice for it. Hints Your cyborg has been really great lately. Your wife loves it. It saved the world. It's nice of you to take this occasion to show the cyborg how much it means to you all with a festival.

meaningMnemonic: If you see a spirit with an axe , you better pray for your life. Spirits only hold axes if they're thinking about murder, so pray as hard as you can to try and get it to spare you. Hints Imagine trying to pray as hard as you can as a spirit with an axe closes in on you. Can you hold your prayer concentration long enough?
readingMnemonic: You pray and pray and pray and nothing happens. You stop praying and dare to open your eyes. There is a key ( き ) in front of you. Grab the key and hold it before you and pray for the spirit to take it. Moments later, both the key and the spirit are gone. Hints I guess the key was prayer all along. ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)

meaningMnemonic: If there’s grass on the ground and fins in your hand , you need to raise that hand up to the sky. You’re in the middle of a fisherman’s ritual, which can only be performed on grassy ground. You take fish fins from the previous year, and raise them up to the sky in order to ensure a good fishing harvest. Hints Feel the grass in your toes and the fins in your hand as you raise them up to the sky. See the sun glistening off the fins as you raise them up in the air.
readingMnemonic: This ritual only works in one part of the world however. It absolutely must be performed in Little Kyo to ( きょ ). The way Little Kyoto lines up with the sun and the sky and all that astrological junk makes it the best place for you to raise fish fins up in the air. Hints Imagine yourself going through the same process as before, only this time imagine yourself in Little Kyoto. Little Kyoto is really little, so make sure you're in the right spot.

meaningMnemonic: All the world 's shellfish are yours to receive . Hints They're all for you. You're the king of the shellfish. Look at all of them, the entire world's shellfish, and they're all yours to receive.
readingMnemonic: Why do you want to receive all these shellfish? Because it's the mora l ( もら ) thing to do. Oh benevolent, moral king of all the world's shellfish, please receive us. Hints Picture yourself as some enlightened, moral king of all the world's shellfish, with your sole duty to receive and take in all the world's shellfish into your flock.

meaningMnemonic: Whatever people say to you will be carved by a blade into your heart . Sounds cruel, but it's a way to make you recognize their power. Hints How could you not acknowledge somebody if every word they said was carved into your heart? It's not particularly painful, but it does make you quite uncomfortable.
readingMnemonic: Having their words carved into your heart makes you recognize the authority of many people. But the only one you could ever truly acknowledge , is Nin tendo ( にん ). Hints You're one of the biggest Nintendo fans out there, so how could you not acknowledge their greatness? No matter what is carved into your heart, Nintendo will always occupy a special place.

meaningMnemonic: The next shellfish will be yours, but this shellfish will be mine. These are the resources we have to share and distribute. Hints Our resources are based around a system of trading shellfish. It's not that weird, plenty of ancient societies used shellfish as their main resource!
readingMnemonic: You save up all of your resources so you can buy a shee p ( し ). You bring a big sack of your shellfish resources to the market and finally get to pick out that sheep you've had your eyes on for months. Hints Of course you're going to use your resources to get a sheep. You're living in a time when shellfish are used to trade for goods and services!

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the radical are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. Righteousness is as righteousness does, right? Hints Go on, put that righteous radical knowledge to use!
readingMnemonic: Such righteousness ! Well, at least according to the king who thinks he's being righteous. His version of righteousness is to send anyone who disagrees with him to the gui llotine ( ぎ ). Hints "THIS IS NOT RIGHTEOUSNESS!" you yell, just before the guillotine comes down on your neck.

meaningMnemonic: Under a tree , a broken arrow protrudes from a turkey . It was fighting for the rights of its fellow turkeys, and was mortally wounded in the process. Hints Imagine comforting this turkey as it leans against the tree, breathing its final breaths. "I lay down my life for the rights of my people…" it gasps. What a noble turkey.
readingMnemonic: "You have rights , so I won't shoot you like this turkey," says the voice of Ken ( けん ) the samurai, from above you in the tree. Hints Ken jumps down and picks the turkey up, the broken arrow sticking out of its neck. "Turkeys do not have rights, my friend. Just let this one go."

meaningMnemonic: A tsunami is coming for the cliff made of tofu , but there is a special sect that protects this tofu cliff. Hints This sect of the tofu-lovers club takes their duties very seriously and they must protect this tofu cliff at all costs.
readingMnemonic: All of the members of the sect are standing on the cliff, their hands raised, and right as the tsunami is about to collide with them, they shout, " Hah ( は )!" and it's repelled! The tsunami sinks and rolls back out to sea — the tofu cliff is safe! Hints Oh, do you want to be a member of the tofu sect? Hah! Don't make me laugh. If you have to ask to be a member of a sect, you'll never get in.

meaningMnemonic: You use a special spear in winter to give yourself the power to do all of your task s. Hints It's hard to get a task done in winter. That's why you have this spear to power and motivate you.
readingMnemonic: Your task is to spear this cow. " Moo ( む )!" it yells at you and runs away. You need to make dinner though... that's your task, so you better catch up to that cow and put an end to its mooing. Hints The moo haunts you as you finish your task. Luckily this spear is helping you keep going even though this task is really difficult.

meaningMnemonic: Some of your grain has just been taken by a guard . This is the tax you pay for living in this town. Back in the day, grain was used like currency, so it makes sense that guards went around collecting grain tax. Hints Can you imagine a guard coming to your door and demanding you pay your grain tax?
readingMnemonic: You have to pay this tax , because if you don't the guard will cut you down with his special German saber, a zei ber ( ぜい ). "Don't you hear vat I zei? Pay ze tax or I vill zlei you vis my zeiber!" he shouts. Hints You don't want to be sliced with the zeiber, so you listen to vat he zei-zei-zeis and pay the tax.

meaningMnemonic: Taking out your thread , you sew together the public 's heart s to make them whole again. Hints The world has been in turmoil and the public has been suffering, but it's time to stop splitting our hearts apart and fighting. It's time to be whole again.
readingMnemonic: Once their hearts are whole , the public's sou l ( そう ) becomes one! Hints Suddenly people who were fighting for years are crying and holding one another. Their souls recognize each other, they're healed, and the whole nation is finally seeing eye to eye.

meaningMnemonic: A truth occasion is reality . This word is also used a lot as an adverb (with or without the particle に ) to mean actually or really .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The つ is shortened to っ .

sentences.japanese: 実際、宇宙人が人ごみに混じっていても、だれも気が付かないだろう。
sentences.english: Actually, I'd say nobody would notice even if an alien mixed in with the crowd.

sentences.japanese: あの男の実際の任務については、だれも知らないんだ。
sentences.english: Nobody knows that man's real mission.

sentences.japanese: 今現在、実際にトーフグは何名の顧客を抱えているのですか？
sentences.english: How many clients does Tofugu actually have at the moment?

meaningMnemonic: Your feeling s are in your heart . When your feelings are in your heart they are pure feelings. You can be happy for people and feel admiration for their successes. This is a great feeling to have in your heart. 感心 expresses that you are being impressed by someone's effort, skill, or good behavior. You'll hear it when someone does something praiseworthy and you genuinely admire it, like 感心した (I’m impressed).
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.english: can be impressed by something, can be impressed by someone

sentences.english: to be impressed by

sentences.japanese: 感心しない
sentences.english: to not think highly of something

sentences.english: to be impressed by something, to be impressed by someone

sentences.english: You have such an admirable child.

sentences.japanese: 毎日勉強するなんて、感心、感心。
sentences.english: I'm so impressed that you study every single day.

sentences.japanese: ケイティには、いつも感心させられっぱなしです。
sentences.english: Katie never ceases to impress me.

meaningMnemonic: You know how 宇宙 is space ? Well, a person from space is an alien .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will also help to know how to read the word 宇宙 on its own, too.

sentences.japanese: 宇宙人と友達になってはいけないと言われて、余計になりたくなった。
sentences.english: When I was told not to be friends with aliens, it made me want to do it even more.

sentences.japanese: 平たく言えば、私達も宇宙人だよね。
sentences.english: To put it simply, we're aliens too, aren't we?

sentences.japanese: コウイチの写真は、火星で干ばつと大恐慌の犠牲となった宇宙人たちを正直に、かつ同情を込めてとらえている。
sentences.english: Koichi’s photographs honestly and sympathetically portray aliens who were victims of drought and the Great Depression on Mars.

meaningMnemonic: 外れる is "to come off" or "to be off." And this is its noun form — a miss , aka something that's off the mark . Whatever it is, it's completely off the original goal or intended target. This word refers to something that falls outside of what's expected, central, or correct. Like something that didn't match your hopes or expectations — a losing lottery ticket or a disappointing purchase. It can also describe a place on the periphery or the outskirts — since you're "off the mark" from somewhere more central.
readingMnemonic: You shoot, but it's a miss . Way off the mark . Better put on your haz mat ( はず ) suit because you hit a toxic waste barrel instead of the target. Put your hazmat suits on, everyone!

sentences.english: far north, the northern outskirts

sentences.japanese: 仲間外れ
sentences.english: being left out

sentences.japanese: 期待外れ
sentences.english: a disappointment

sentences.english: the outskirts of the town

sentences.english: the outskirts of Seattle

sentences.japanese: ニューヨークの外れ
sentences.english: the outskirts of New York City

sentences.english: No matter how many times I threw the darts, they wouldn't hit the dartboard, and in the end, they were all misses.

sentences.japanese: 先生の予想は完全に外れでした。
sentences.english: The teacher's prediction was completely off the mark.

sentences.japanese: 男は森の外れの小さな家に住んでいた。
sentences.english: The man lived in a small house on the forest's periphery.

sentences.japanese: 王女は、季節外れのドレスを着ていた。
sentences.english: The princess was wearing a dress that doesn't suit the season.

meaningMnemonic: Your big enemy is your worst enemy. Your arch enemy . 大敵 is for a powerful or dangerous opponent, whether it's a formidable adversary in battle or competition, or something abstract, like calling carelessness your great enemy .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. Both kanji have a couple different on'yomi readings though, so here's a mnemonic to help you remember which ones to pick: Your arch enemy is the tie techie ( たいてき ). Who's the tie techie? He's the tech support guy at work who always wears the same tie and never helps you. He just says "try restarting your computer" to every problem, which isn't helpful. He's not just a great enemy, he's basically your nemesis. You hate that tie techie.

sentences.japanese: ワニカニの大敵はだれだと思いますか？
sentences.english: Who do you think is Wanikani's rival?

sentences.japanese: オレたちの大敵が、ついに敗北を認めたぞ。
sentences.english: Our arch enemy finally acknowledged their defeat.

sentences.japanese: 分かっていると思うけど、油断大敵だよ。「サルも木から落ちる」って言うだろう？
sentences.english: As you all know, carelessness is man's greatest enemy. People say "even monkeys fall from trees," right?

meaningMnemonic: You have rights to profit ! This is a right you have!

meaningMnemonic: A reality feeling is what you get when something feels real. For example, when you're expecting a baby, you may understand that you're becoming a parent, but not truly have that realization until the baby is born or you hold them in your arms. It's the sense of something feeling real beyond theory or explanation — when it truly sinks in.

sentences.english: Tom's name was mentioned at the time, wasn't it?

sentences.japanese: 自分がヒゲ大賞の候補に挙がっているなんて、信じられないよ。
sentences.english: I can’t believe that I’m nominated for the Mustache Award.

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means blame so this also means to blame . Additionally, this can also mean to criticize , to reproach , or to accuse .
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Are you going to blame me for eating your ce lery ( せ )? You should know I'm the wrong person to blame because I don't even like celery!

sentences.japanese: 「自分でちゃんとチェックするべきだったよ。」「そんなに自分を責めないで。あなたのせいじゃないわよ。」
sentences.english: "I should have checked it out myself." "Don’t blame yourself. It wasn’t your fault."

sentences.japanese: 台風で電車のダイヤが混乱してただけなんだから、マイケルさんを責めるのはおかしいよ。
sentences.english: The typhoon disrupted the train schedule, so blaming Michael is unreasonable.

sentences.japanese: 子どもが熱を出したんだけど、判断を誤って病院に連れて行かなかったら肺炎になっちゃってね。後で妻からひどく責められたよ。
sentences.english: Our kid had a fever, but I messed up and didn't take him to the hospital, so he ended up with pneumonia. My wife later reproached me harshly.

meaningMnemonic: The kanji means come true , and this is the intransitive verb version of that, making this to come true or to be fulfilled .
readingMnemonic: This is a verb, so it uses the kun'yomi reading. Luckily, you already learned this with the kanji, so you should be good to go here!

sentences.japanese: 願いが叶う
sentences.english: a wish comes true

sentences.japanese: 夢が叶う
sentences.english: a dream comes true

sentences.japanese: 希望が叶う
sentences.english: a hope comes true

sentences.english: one's love is reciprocated

sentences.english: I hope this wish comes true someday.

sentences.japanese: どうせ、叶わぬ恋だったんだよ。
sentences.english: Anyway, it was a love that was never meant to be.

sentences.japanese: 大丈夫、あきらめなければ、夢はきっと叶うよ！
sentences.english: Don't worry, if you don't give up, your dreams will surely come true!

meaningMnemonic: 埋める is "to bury." 合わせる is "to unify together." If you bury somebody in order to unify them with you, you're almost certainly trying to compensate for something.
readingMnemonic: The readings come from 埋める and 合わせる . Combine them into one big happy word.

sentences.japanese: 病気で休んだ分を休日に働いて埋め合わせるつもりだ。
sentences.english: I plan to work on my days off to make up for the time I took off due to illness.

sentences.japanese: 知性が足りないのを金で埋め合わせることはできると思う？
sentences.english: Do you think it's possible to compensate for a lack of intelligence with money?

sentences.japanese: どうにかこの損失を埋め合わせることはできないだろうか。
sentences.english: Can’t we make up for this loss in some way or another?

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means continue , so 続ける means to continue something . It's a transitive verb, so it takes a direct object. You can 続ける your work, for example, and you should 続ける your WaniKani lessons at a pace that works for you! Although it has the same 続 kanji, this word is a bit different from 続く , which is used for when something just continues on its own (like rain, or trends). It can be hard to remember the difference, so here's a mnemonic to help you with 続ける : You only care ( ける ) about things that you can continue through your own actions. For those other things that just continue on their own, you're like, That's coo ' ( く ), but you’re not that interested.
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as 続く , so be sure to know that so you can know this.

sentences.japanese: これからもずっとワニカニを続けるつもりです♡
sentences.english: I will continue WaniKani forever ♡

sentences.japanese: どうしてあなた達は私のことを批判し続けるのですか？
sentences.english: Why do you all keep criticizing me?

sentences.japanese: 一日中寝続けられるので、週末は最高だ。
sentences.english: Weekends are awesome because I can continue to sleep all day long.

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means decrease so the verb vocab version is to decrease something . You can differentiate this from 減る because with this one, you are the one that is going to be doing the decreasing. The rush ( らす ) of decreasing something fills your veins.
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as 減る , so if you know that reading you should know this one.

sentences.japanese: 先生に宿題をちょっとだけ減らしてもらいました。
sentences.english: I had my teacher decrease the number of homework assignments I was given.

sentences.japanese: クリームの量を減らすようお願いしたんですが、聞き入れてもらえませんでした。
sentences.english: I asked them to reduce the amount of cream, but they didn't accept my request.

sentences.japanese: その疫病は、河豚の数をそれまでの水準の半分に減らした。
sentences.english: The plague reduced the number of blowfish to half its previous level.

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means envy so the verb version is to envy someone.
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You haven't learned this reading yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You're really starting to envy those ura nium Ya nkees ( うらや ). That's the new Yankees team hopped up on uranium that were created in a lab. Even though they're gross and hulk-ish, they're really good at baseball, so you're jealous of them.

sentences.japanese: コウイチは、世界が羨む男だ。
sentences.english: Koichi is a man the world envies.

sentences.japanese: 人は他人の幸せを羨みがちだ。
sentences.english: People have the tendency to envy others' happiness.

sentences.japanese: いつか誰もが羨む名声と富を手に入れたいです。
sentences.english: One day, I want to acquire wealth and fame that anyone would envy.

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means establish so the verb vocab version is to establish , or to set up . 設ける is a formal word that suggests setting up something in order to prep for future needs or events. If you want to ensure smooth operation or governance, for example, you might set up rules ( ルールを設ける ) or establish an office ( オフィスを設ける ). You can even use it to say you’ll arrange a drinking party ( 酒の席を設ける ), in which case it probably means the party has a more formal purpose like networking or discussion.
readingMnemonic: What are you going to establish ? How about a system for mow ing ( もう ) lawns? It's very important that lawns are mowed according to an established system, you know. How do you mow yours?

sentences.japanese: トーフグがついに日本支店を設けるというウワサを聞いたんだけど、本当かな？
sentences.english: I heard a rumor that Tofugu is finally going to set up a branch in Japan, but I wonder if it's true.

sentences.japanese: 社長、今度はオフィスにサウナを設けるつもりらしいですよ。
sentences.english: I heard that the president is planning to set up a sauna in the office this time.

sentences.japanese: コウイチは、新しい従業員規則を設けることを検討しているようです。
sentences.english: Apparently Koichi is considering establishing new rules for his employees.

meaningMnemonic: Double frustration would cause anyone to get irritated , to get annoyed , or to grow impatient .
readingMnemonic: This isn’t the reading you learned with the kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You don’t just get irritated, you get ira-ira -tated ( いらいら ). That's the next level up from irritated. This word is often written in katakana or hiragana, but you'll sometimes see it in kanji too, so it's worth knowing!

sentences.japanese: あの人、いつも苛々しているね。
sentences.english: That person is always irritated, huh?

sentences.japanese: 運転しながら苛々しないでよ。
sentences.english: Don't get impatient while you're driving.

sentences.japanese: 私だって苛々したくてしてる訳じゃないよ。
sentences.english: It's not like I’m trying to get annoyed.

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means give birth so the verb vocab version is to give birth . You know another 産む as well ( 生む ). This 産む is more sciency, but both are good to know.
readingMnemonic: You know another "to give birth" word ( 生む ). Guess what!? They share readings!

sentences.japanese: あの人、去年の冬に赤ちゃんを産んだばかりなのに今年の秋にもまた赤ちゃんを産むんですって。
sentences.english: I heard that person just gave birth to a baby last winter and that she'll have another one this fall.

sentences.japanese: カマキリが産んだたまごの中からたくさんの赤ちゃんカマキリが出てきました。
sentences.english: A lot of baby mantises came out of the egg that the mantis laid.

sentences.japanese: よし、もう一度いきむ準備はいいかい？君は双子の赤ちゃんを産むんだよ！ 大丈夫、大丈夫。頑張れ！君ならできるよ！
sentences.english: Okay. You ready to push again? You are going to have twins! Okay, okay, come on, you can do it. You can do it!

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means increase , so the vocabulary verb version means to increase . This is when something is just increasing on its own, and you're not doing the increasing. You know this because you like to err ( える ) on the side of caution and not touch anything when it's increasing, therefore you're not doing any of the increasing yourself (it's just happening). This is an everyday word that refers to an increase in number or quantity, but keep in mind that it cannot be used to express an increase in degree.
readingMnemonic: It would be foo lish ( ふ ) of you to touch anything while things are increasing anyways. You don't want to mess up a good thing, do you? Don't be a fool.

sentences.japanese: ここ2、3年、ビエトが一日に飲むお酒、かなり増えてるんだよね。
sentences.english: Over the past few years, Viet’s daily amount of alcohol has been considerably increasing.

sentences.japanese: もう少し建設的な批判が増えるといいんだけど。
sentences.english: It would be nice if the constructive criticism increased a bit.

sentences.japanese: 母の黒髪に交じった白髪の量が、以前より増えている気がした。
sentences.english: It felt like the number of gray hairs mixed into my mom's black hair had increased since I last saw her.

meaningMnemonic: You examine the problem . In order to do this, you need to inspect it or to examine it. And if you're inspecting people like this, you're probably the police.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.japanese: ほら、あそこで警察が検問しているよ。
sentences.english: Hey look, the police are examining people over there.

sentences.japanese: 警察が私の車を検問している時、ドキドキしました。
sentences.english: While the police were inspecting my car, my heart was racing.

sentences.japanese: 成田空港の検問所で検問している警備員の中には、トレーニング中の警備員もいます。
sentences.english: Some of the security guards who inspect people at Narita Airport's checkpoints are undergoing training.

meaningMnemonic: You 立つ and then 去る . Makes sense, as in order to leave , you'll have to stand up first. 立ち去る describes the physical act of leaving a place, often used when walking away from a scene or departing a place after some kind of incident or event.
readingMnemonic: This combines the readings of two verbs you already know, so you should be good to go here!

sentences.english: to walk away from there

sentences.japanese: 私の前から立ち去る
sentences.english: to walk away from me

sentences.japanese: 何も言わずに立ち去るなんて、ひどいよ。
sentences.english: Walking away without saying a word is not cool.

sentences.english: Leave this place now, quickly!

sentences.japanese: 男はその場を足早に立ち去った。
sentences.english: The man quickly left the spot.

meaningMnemonic: This word ends with a う sound so you can guess it's a verb. The kanji means nothing , and the best way to end up with nothing is either to lose something or to get rid of it. 無くす is a broad word that can be used both when you unintentionally lose something, like 財布を無くしちゃった (I lost my wallet), and when you deliberately do away with something, as in 戦争を無くす (eliminate war).
readingMnemonic: This word uses the kun'yomi, which you already learned when you learned the word 無し .

sentences.japanese: パスポートを無くすなんて信じられないけど、本当にあるんだね...。
sentences.english: I can't believe anyone would lose their passport, but it really does happen...

sentences.english: What do you think caused you to lose your self-confidence?

sentences.english: Even though they had backed up the important data to make sure it wouldn't be lost, somehow even the backup disappeared, leaving the company president speechless.

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means conserve ... but why stop there when you could try to omit everything and to eliminate everything? Just take exactly what you need, conserve it, and omit everything else.
readingMnemonic: You have ( はぶ ) what you have, and omit what you don't need. Perfect life.

sentences.japanese: 最近はとても忙しいので、夕食を作る手間を省いてテイクアウトばかりしています。
sentences.english: I've been very busy these days, so I've been skipping meal prep and just buying to-go dinners.

sentences.japanese: 説明がたくさん省かれていたので理解できませんでした。
sentences.english: A lot of the explanations were left out, so I couldn't understand it.

sentences.japanese: このロボットが多くの人手を省くはずだったが、状況は変化しないままである。
sentences.english: This robot was supposed to save us a lot of labor, but the situation remains unchanged.

meaningMnemonic: You know how 参加 is participation ? Well, make that a verb with する and you have yourself to participate .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Will also help to know the reading of 参加 .

sentences.japanese: ジャズ評論家として、とあるセミナーに参加してきました。
sentences.english: I participated in a seminar as a jazz critic.

sentences.japanese: クラブ活動に参加するかどうかは、任意です。
sentences.english: Participating in club activities is optional.

sentences.japanese: 今週の日曜日、摩天楼の見学ツアーに参加します。
sentences.english: I’m participating in the skyscraper observation tour this Sunday.

meaningMnemonic: You know that 説得 is persuasion , so what is the verb version of that? To persuade .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will also immensely help to know the reading of the word 説得 .

sentences.japanese: ロックミュージシャンになるには、親父を説得する必要がある。

sentences.english: I persuaded my wife not to buy unnecessary things.

sentences.japanese: ベーコンの密売ビジネスから足を洗うよう兄を説得するのは、容易なことではなかった。
sentences.english: It wasn't easy to convince my brother to bail out of the bacon-trafficking business.

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means plan so the verb vocab version is to plan .
readingMnemonic: You say you have something you need to plan ? Coo l, whadda ya ( くわだ ) gonna do?

sentences.japanese: 「何それ？」「わっ！何でもないよ。」「何か企てているでしょう？」
sentences.english: "What is it?" "Ah, nothing!" "You’re planning something, aren’t you?!"

sentences.japanese: クーデターを企てたが、失敗してしまった。
sentences.english: We planned a coup, but it failed.

sentences.japanese: コウイチの暗殺を企てていたワニカニユーザーを、ビエトがこっそり始末したらしいぜ。
sentences.english: Apparently there was a Wanikani user who made an attempt on Koichi's life, but Viet quietly got rid of them.

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means pray and this verb is transitive, so it means to pray for .
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: "You gotta pray for Christmas presents if you want Santa to bring you some!" " I know ( いの ), I know," you reply as you begin to pray for presents. You should say this out loud to remember it better.

sentences.japanese: ハリケーンのひがい者のために祈りました。
sentences.english: I prayed for the hurricane victims.

sentences.english: I pray that you will pass the national examinations successfully.

sentences.japanese: 日本の国技である相撲が、かつては米の豊作を祈る儀式だったことを知ってる日本人がたくさんいるとは思えないな。
sentences.english: I don’t think many Japanese people know Japan’s national sport "sumo" used to be a ritual to pray for a bountiful rice harvest.

meaningMnemonic: You know how 乱れる is "to be in disorder"? Well, now you're the one causing this. So, by doing this you are going to put in disorder , to throw out of order , or to disturb whatever it is. Just imagine all the people who will try to sue ( す ) you for your actions.
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as 乱れる , so hopefully you know it already.

sentences.japanese: そういう発言がみんなの和を乱しているってこと、気づいてないの？
sentences.english: Don't you realize that such comments disturb everyone's harmony?

sentences.japanese: ADHDの子どもは、生活のリズムを乱されることをイヤがる子が多いです。
sentences.english: Many kids with ADHD don't like having the rhythm of their lives thrown out of order.

sentences.japanese: 髪を乱して走ったが、結局予定の飛行機には間に合わなかった。
sentences.english: I ran with my hair in disarray, but in the end I didn't make my scheduled flight.

meaningMnemonic: This word consists of kanji with hiragana attached. Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means receive , making this to receive something , or alternatively, to get something from someone or to be given something .
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You learned that reading with the kanji, so you should be good to go here!

sentences.english: to receive from one's parents

sentences.english: to receive from someone

sentences.english: Could I receive some advice about this?

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means cut off . What happens when you do the action of cutting someone off? You're going to refuse them whatever it is they want.
readingMnemonic: Deciding to refuse something unfortunately starts a coat war (like a pillow fight, but everyone hits each other with coats instead of pillows). Coats to the ready, and let the coat war commence!

sentences.japanese: その仕事、断るべきだと思う？
sentences.english: Do you think I should refuse the job?

sentences.japanese: ビエトは次期国務長官に任命されたが、断った。
sentences.english: Viet was appointed as the next Secretary of State, but he refused.

sentences.english: I was asked to be the chief umpire for a baseball game, but I rejected the offer. I would have done it if it was for the chief referee of a soccer game though.

meaningMnemonic: What do you establish and determine in your every day life? A setting. When you make that into a verb, you have the word to set , as in setting the temperature of the AC, setting your password, or setting your computer to dark mode. 設定する is a little formal, but does get commonly used for device, system, and game settings. It's also often used in more official contexts, like for setting prices for products or establishing project goals.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Careful because the 設 gets shortened to せっ .

sentences.japanese: あなたの新しいビジネス用のメールアカウントを、グーグルに設定しました。
sentences.english: I set up a new business mail account in Google for you.

sentences.japanese: クーラーはいつも何度に設定していますか？
sentences.english: What temperature do you usually set your air conditioner to?

sentences.japanese: 今日中に全てのアカウントの二段階認証を設定しないと、会社を首になるんです。
sentences.english: I have to set up two-factor authentications with all the accounts I have by the end of day or I'll get fired.

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means bind or tie , so the verb vocab version is to tie . Tying is also a great way to connect things, so this verb sometimes means that too. At its core, 結ぶ is about bringing things together and creating a connection. It can be physical, like tying a string, but it's also commonly used in abstract ways, like forming relationships or establishing contracts.
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: You decide to tie a ribbon on a moose ( むす ). Why? sentences.english: The way you tie your hair back with a ribbon like that is cute.

meaningMnemonic: If your eye s are awake then you're going to wake up . Your eyes are usually the first thing to awaken when you're waking up, you know? This word can also mean to awaken but it's like when you to come to your senses, not literally waking up.
readingMnemonic: The readings for this word are both kun'yomi readings. You haven’t learned this reading for 覚 yet, and in this case it also gets rendaku’d, so bear that in mind. Anyway, here’s a mnemonic to help you: If you start to wake up in the middle of the night, it’s because of the C za r ( ざ ) you met that had banned sitting. This cruel, ruthless Czar keeps appearing in your nightmares, causing you to wake up incessantly. Terrifying.

sentences.japanese: このライフハックを使うと、朝、すっきり目覚めることができます。
sentences.english: If you use this life hack, you can wake up feeling refreshed in the morning.

sentences.english: It seems that Ken has finally become aware of what it means to become company president.

sentences.english: I was nodding off in the train, and when I woke up, I was surprised to find myself at an unfamiliar station.

meaningMnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means task so what's the verb vocab version? Well, when you do a task, you are going to work as or to serve as something to do that task.
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: To work as my secretary, you will have to complete a task. A task where you bring me two toe s ( つと )! Don't ask me why! You want to serve as my assistant, right? Just get me those two toes then!

sentences.english: My father worked as a police officer for forty years until last year.

sentences.english: Mr. Tamura was employed as Ms. Tanaka’s private secretary for one year, but it didn’t really work out.

meaningMnemonic: Remember how 動詞 means "verb"? When the verb is done to some other thing, it's a transitive verb . That means it takes a direct object. Verbs like 食べる , 使う , and 上げる are transitive verbs because they need a direct object, an "other" thing, to receive their action.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

sentences.english: Transitive verbs take objects.

sentences.english: Please change all of these transitive verbs into intransitive verbs.

meaningMnemonic: A mouth flute ... Normal flutes you blow air through to make a sound. How do you blow air through your mouth to make a sound? By whistling .
